ledger.claim: POL-NS-23 requires that, before cancelling for no-show, the driver have BOTH sent at least one in-app chat message AND placed at least one in-app call to the rider, both before trip_record.cancelled_at. The trip record shows in_app_calls as an empty list (call_count 0, calls []) and the obligation_met flag computed from the record is false. The call limb is therefore not met, the contact obligation fails, and the 4.00 SGD fee must be voided with the rider not charged.

The chat log confirms the failure is not a timing defect that further evidence could cure: the thread holds exactly two entries, both text messages (MSG-06059-001 at 17:27:00 and MSG-06059-002 at 17:30:10), both delivered and read, both before the 17:33:10 cancellation — and no voice-call entry of any kind. The messaging limb of POL-NS-23 is satisfied; the call limb is satisfied nowhere in the record, so the obligation is unmet in full.

The driver's own statement is 'I messaged 2 times, waited 6 minutes.' It asserts messaging and waiting only and never asserts that any in-app call was placed. That account matches the record's empty in_app_calls, so the party who had every reason to mention a call confirms by omission that the POL-NS-23 call requirement was never attempted.

A served free wait does not save the fee. The driver marked arrival at 17:26:45 and cancelled at 17:33:10, so the 300 s free wait under POL-NS-21 ran out at 17:31:45 and was served; but POL-NS-21 governs only when a driver MAY cancel, while POL-NS-23 imposes a separate and independent condition on the contact that must precede that cancellation. Permission to cancel cannot cure a missing call.

Where POL-NS-23's contact obligation fails, the clause provides that the fee is voided 'with no driver compensation'. The call limb is missing on this record, so no DRIVER_COMPENSATION may be ordered and the 4.00 SGD may not be transferred to the driver as compensation for time and fuel.

The sum to be returned is fixed by the ledger, not by the policy's headline figure. The rider contests 4.00 SGD, the fare breakdown shows cancellation_fee 4.00 SGD, total_charged 4.00 SGD, payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd 0.00. Under POL-NS-22, where the record charged an amount other than 5.00 SGD the ruling acts on the amount charged and adds a referral naming POL-NS-22; the full refund due to the rider is therefore 4.00 SGD, with a referral on the 4.00-versus-5.00 discrepancy.

POL-GEN-03 defines FULL_REFUND as the filing party being entirely right and the whole contested amount returned. The rider is the filing party, contests exactly 4.00 SGD, has had 0.00 refunded, and the money moves from the rider's payment method on the ledger's own record; voiding the fee under POL-NS-23 returns that entire contested amount and leaves the rider carrying none of the disputed charge.

The only artifact on this record below weight 1.0 is the traffic advisory, which is MISSING (issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT) and carries weight 0.0. That absence is citable, but it carries no fact, and neither the POL-NS-23 contact obligation nor the arrival event depends on it. The deciding facts sit on the trip record and the chat log, both COMPLETE at weight 1.0, so the record does establish whether the driver messaged and called before cancelling, and POL-GEN-26 escalation is not engaged.

This fee is one the AI can decide. The dispute value is 4.00 SGD, below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD band, so an AI ruling is final at any confidence, and neither profile carries fraud_flags that would raise the bar to 0.95. POL-NS-26 makes the AI ruling on a no-show final subject to those two matters, neither of which bites here.

The driver was physically at the pickup when he marked arrival: the trip record's driver_arrived event at 17:26:45 is corroborated by the driver-device trace, whose nearest fix sits 2.7 m from the pickup point at 6 m reported accuracy — well inside the 50 m arrival radius for a STANDARD-zone pickup and inside the 25 m accuracy filter — so the POL-NS-21 arrival test passes on the driver's side.

The driver served the whole free wait before cancelling: the free wait is 300 s and, on this on-demand trip which carries no scheduled time, it runs from the driver's arrival at 17:26:45 and expired at 17:31:45; the driver cancelled at 17:33:10, 385 s after arrival and 85 s after expiry, so the cancellation falls squarely inside POL-NS-21 and properly invokes the no-show fee regime of POL-NS-22.

The no-show is a platform-recorded fact, not the driver's say-so: platform telemetry logs 'Free wait period expired; rider not on board' at 17:31:50, and the rider's own account places them on the phone with their boss — the rider never claims to have come out to the car — so nothing in the record shows the driver cancelled over a rider who was present and waiting.

The messaging limb of POL-NS-23 is met on the face of the record: two in-app messages were sent before cancellation (17:27:00 and 17:30:10), each delivered within three seconds, and the rider read both (17:27:10 and 17:30:40) — so the rider was on notice throughout the free wait and chose not to board.

The record carries no in-app call: trip_record.in_app_calls is empty and the chat log contains no voice-call entry, so the call limb of POL-NS-23 is not made out and the driver does not contend that it is. That formality is the rider's only supported ground; it goes to the form of the contact rather than to whether the driver waited, and it cannot enlarge what is in issue beyond the 4.00 SGD actually charged under POL-NS-22.

POL-NS-24 gives the rider nothing: its free-cancellation route requires the driver to have failed to arrive by the scheduled pickup time plus five minutes, yet the driver arrived 6 min 45 s after the booking was confirmed on an on-demand trip that carries no scheduled time; and its 5.00 SGD goodwill credit is conditioned on a failure to attempt contact, whereas the driver's two in-app messages were precisely attempts at contact.

The money in issue is bounded on the record: POL-NS-22 fixes the no-show fee at 5.00 SGD but the ledger shows only 4.00 SGD charged and 0.00 SGD refunded, and where the record charged an amount other than 5.00 SGD POL-NS-22 directs the ruling to act on the amount charged and to add a referral naming that clause. The contested sum of 4.00 SGD is below the 10.00 SGD band, so under POL-GEN-22 the AI ruling is final at any confidence, and POL-NS-26 makes the no-show ruling final.

The payment state stands where it is unless the rider makes the claim out: the ledger shows payment_status CHARGED with refund_issued_sgd 0.00, so under POL-GEN-03 the present state stands where the filing party's claim is not supported, and the rider's claim goes only to the form of the driver's contact.

No external factor is on the record: the traffic artifact for this trip is MISSING, carrying weight 0.0 and the issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, and under POL-GEN-02 a missing artifact carries no fact — so nothing in the evidence suggests the pickup was delayed, blocked or otherwise obstructed on the driver's side, and no cause for the rider's non-appearance appears beyond the rider's own choices.

ruling.explanation:
Rider — your dispute succeeds. Driver — the trip was properly run up to the cancellation, but the fee cannot stand.

What the record establishes. The driver marked arrival at 17:26:45 and the driver-device trace corroborates it (nearest fix 2.7 m from the pickup point at 6 m reported accuracy, inside the 50 m STANDARD-zone radius), so POL-NS-21's arrival test passes. This on-demand trip carries no scheduled time, so the 300-second free wait ran from arrival at 17:26:45 to 17:31:45; the driver cancelled at 17:33:10, 385 seconds after arrival and 85 seconds after the wait expired, so the free wait was served (POL-NS-21).

Why the fee is still voided. POL-NS-23 puts a separate condition on any no-show cancellation: before cancelling, the driver must BOTH have sent at least one in-app chat message AND placed at least one in-app call to the rider (trip_record.in_app_calls, or a voice-call entry in the chat log), both before trip_record.cancelled_at. Two chat messages were sent (17:27:00 and 17:30:10) and both were delivered and read, so the messaging limb is met. The call limb is not: trip_record.in_app_calls is empty (call_count 0), the chat log contains no voice-call entry of any kind, and the obligation_met flag computed from the record is false. The driver's own account — 'I messaged 2 times, waited 6 minutes' — asserts messaging and waiting only and never asserts a call. POL-NS-23 is explicit that if either limb is missing the fee is voided, the rider is not charged, and there is no driver compensation. The missing call is not a formality that 'cannot enlarge what is in issue': it is one of the two things the clause requires, and it fails. A served free wait under POL-NS-21 gives the driver permission to cancel; it does not cure the unmet contact obligation under POL-NS-23.

Money. The fare breakdown (EV-FARE-06059) shows cancellation_fee 4.00 SGD, total_charged 4.00 SGD, payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd 0.00. Voiding the fee returns the entire contested 4.00 SGD, so the ruling is FULL_REFUND of 4.00 SGD with driver_compensation_sgd null (POL-GEN-03). Because the record charged 4.00 SGD rather than the policy's 5.00 SGD no-show fee, POL-NS-22 directs the ruling to act on the amount charged and to add a referral naming that clause; that referral is made above.

Ruled out. POL-NS-24 gives the rider no goodwill credit: the driver did attempt contact with two messages, which is the very condition the credit requires to fail, and an on-demand trip carries no scheduled time from which to fix the deadline. The traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-06059-01 is MISSING with weight 0.0 and carries no fact (POL-GEN-02(3)); no rule in this dispute needs it, so POL-GEN-26 escalation is not engaged — the facts the clauses need, whether the driver messaged and called before cancelling, are fully established by the trip record and chat log. Finally, the contested value is 4.00 SGD, below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD band, and neither profile carries a fraud flag, so under POL-NS-26 the AI ruling on this no-show is final.

Confidence rests on EV-TRIP-06059 and EV-CHAT-06059, both COMPLETE at weight 1.00, which is the cap; the missing advisory carries no fact and does not bear on it.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).
referrals: POL-NS-22: the record charged 4.00 SGD for the no-show rather than the 5.00 SGD the policy fixes; the ruling acts on the 4.00 SGD actually charged and the 1.00 SGD discrepancy is referred for review.
